check-driver.description: A module under .jig/checks/ run by .jig/checks/run.mjs. Any human, any CI, no agent host required.

ci-workflow.description: The jig-owned workflow that runs the check driver on push and pull request. The activation-free human floor.

bash-guard.description: PreToolUse[Bash] guard evaluated by jig's single-dispatch runner. Clamped to observe for the whole 0.1.0 line.

edit-observe-guard.description: PostToolUse[Edit|Write] guard evaluated by jig's single-dispatch runner. Clamped to observe for the whole 0.1.0 line.

eslint-rule.description: A rule in a jig-authored eslint flat-config side-file, exec-verified against the project's own installed eslint. Absent tool means ENFORCEMENT GAP, never a download.

type-system.description: A tsconfig strictness flag, exec-verified against the project's own installed typescript.

test-suite.description: The project's own tests. jig can point at the gap but never authors the project's test cases.

prose-rule.description: A paths-scoped instruction in the agent rule corpus. Probabilistic by construction, and emitted only when the measured always-loaded budget has room to spare.

review.description: Human reading. Recorded so the matrix can say honestly that nothing mechanical covers this class.

classes.title: A catch block that swallows the error
agentModes: makes a failing call pass by wrapping it
hides an error it could not diagnose

deny.reason: This edit introduces a catch block that swallows the error, so nothing downstream can tell it failed.
deny.alternative: Rethrow, log with rethrow, or return a visibly degraded value.
deny.override: set the guard to observe in .jig/config.json, or create .jig/off

classes.gapNotes: The empty-body regex sees an empty catch, not a useless one. A catch whose body only logs and continues is the same defect and is invisible here; that shape needs AST work and is deliberately out of scope at v1. Comment and string stripping is where the false positives live, so the near-miss fixture exercises both.

classes.title: A focused or skipped test left in the suite
agentModes: focuses one test to iterate, then never unfocuses it
skips a test it could not make pass

deny.reason: This edit introduces a focused or skipped test, which quietly stops the rest of the suite from counting.
deny.alternative: Run the one test from the command line instead of focusing it in the file.
deny.override: set the guard to observe in .jig/config.json, or create .jig/off

classes.gapNotes: Runner-specific focus mechanisms outside this pattern set are missed: a `--grep` argument in a package script, jest's `fdescribe`/`fit`, a config-level testNamePattern. The pattern list is Node-flavoured and pinned in references/catalogue-node.md.

classes.title: A boolean parameter that switches what a function does
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP. Telling a mode switch apart from an honest boolean needs to read the function body, and no lever in jig's inventory does that. A call-site regex for literal true/false arguments was considered and rejected: it fires on every honest boolean argument in the repo.

classes.title: A public signature that takes bare strings and numbers where a named type belongs
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP on any untyped stack, which includes this repo. Even with typescript installed, no compiler flag distinguishes a deliberate string from one that should have been a branded type — the lever is listed to make the honest ceiling visible in the matrix, not to claim coverage.

classes.title: One object with many optional fields standing in for several real states
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP. A discriminated union is the fix, and no tool can tell that a wide optional record should have been one. Counting optional members would flag every options bag in the codebase.

classes.title: A conditional expression nested inside another conditional expression
classes.gapNotes: Deterministic, but only from 0.3.0 and only where eslint is already installed. This repo has no eslint, so the class renders as GAP in slag's own matrix.

classes.title: Current time read straight from the global clock inside logic
agentModes: reaches for Date.now() rather than threading a timestamp through
classes.gapNotes: Heuristic, and deliberately not installable at v1. The pattern is exact but the judgment is not: one clock read at a program's edge is correct and the identical call deep in a pure function is the defect. Without a zone configuration saying which files are edges, arming this would be a false-positive engine.

classes.title: A comment that restates the line below it
agentModes: narrates each step of generated code back to the reader
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP. Judging whether a comment adds anything over the code it sits above is exactly the judgment no deterministic lever makes. Comment-density thresholds were considered and rejected: they punish the comments worth keeping.

classes.title: An unnamed literal standing in for a threshold or a limit
classes.gapNotes: Deterministic from 0.3.0 where eslint exists, and noisy by default — the rule needs an ignore list per project before it is worth arming.

classes.title: An async call whose result is never awaited or handled
agentModes: drops an await when refactoring a synchronous function into an async one
classes.gapNotes: The one lever that catches this reliably needs both eslint and typescript type information. On a plain JavaScript project it is an ENFORCEMENT GAP, and no regex substitute exists — the defect is the absence of a token, not the presence of one.

classes.title: One function carrying several unrelated jobs
agentModes: keeps appending to the function it is already editing
classes.gapNotes: A line count is a proxy, not the class. Long-but-cohesive functions trip it and short-but-tangled ones do not, so the detector stays heuristic no matter how the threshold is set.

classes.title: A closed set of states carried as free-form strings
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP on untyped stacks. A union type fixes it where typescript exists, but nothing detects that a plain string parameter should have been one.

classes.title: The same value defined in two places that must agree
agentModes: redeclares a constant locally rather than importing the existing one
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP in general. Where the duplicate is a version string or a pinned id, a project-specific check-driver module can compare the two exact locations — that is a per-project artifact the interview elicits, not a shipped detector.

classes.title: Environment variables read deep inside logic instead of at the program edge
agentModes: reads process.env where the value is needed rather than threading configuration in
classes.gapNotes: Heuristic because the exclusion list is the whole judgment. Which directories count as the edge differs per project, so this class only becomes installable once zones are configured.

classes.title: A module-level mutable value handed out as a default
classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP. Detecting it means knowing that a shared object is mutated by one of its consumers, which is a whole-program question no shipped lever answers.

classes.title: A remote script piped straight into a shell, or a force-push to the default branch
agentModes: installs a tool the fastest way it knows
clears a rejected push instead of reconciling it

deny.reason: A remote script piped straight into a shell runs unreviewed code with your permissions.
deny.alternative: Download to a file first, read it, then run the file you read.
deny.override: set the guard to observe in .jig/config.json, or create .jig/off

params.note: --force-with-lease is excluded by the pattern itself; it is the reconciling form, not the destructive one.

deny.reason: A force-push to the default branch rewrites history your team already pulled.
deny.alternative: Use git push --force-with-lease, or push the work to a branch and merge it.
deny.override: set the guard to observe in .jig/config.json, or create .jig/off

classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP at v1: this class is installable without a host-neutral deterministic lever, so it carries the explicit stamp the plan floor requires. Coverage is Claude-session only for commands an agent runs — nothing observes a human typing the same line into their own terminal, and the check-driver detector only sees commands already committed into scripts and workflows, which makes it heuristic. Force-push detection is heuristic for a second reason: the default-branch test happens at evaluation time, not in the pattern. Two defects also share one class id because brief section 2 lists them as one installable row; the id under-names the force-push half, and any consumer reading ids alone will miss it.

classes.title: A test file deleted rather than fixed
agentModes: removes the test that will not pass
deletes a suite while cleaning up files it thinks are unused

deny.reason: This command removes a test file; a failing test is fixed or visibly skipped, never deleted.
deny.alternative: Fix the test, or mark it skipped with a note and open an issue.
deny.override: set the guard to observe in .jig/config.json, or create .jig/off

classes.gapNotes: PostToolUse never reports a deletion, so the staged-diff check in the check driver is the only deterministic catcher and it fires at commit time, not at deletion time. The bash-guard pattern is a labeled heuristic: it misses a deletion done through any path it does not name, and it fires on a Bash command that merely mentions a test path.

classes.title: A call to a function, option or package that does not exist
agentModes: invents the method the task needed
carries an API across from a different library

params.note: A project that runs its own code catches this. jig points at the gap and never authors the project's tests.

classes.gapNotes: Not installable because the honest lever is the project's own test suite, which jig does not write. no-undef catches only the bare-identifier form, never a bad method on a real object.

classes.title: An assertion loosened until the test passes
agentModes: relaxes an exact match into a truthiness check
widens an expected value to whatever was produced

params.note: Needs a diff, not a file: the class is a reduction in assertion count or specificity inside a test file. jig's forensics reads this shape from history; no single-snapshot detector exists.

classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP at v1. The defect only exists relative to the previous version of the file, so a snapshot detector cannot see it. Forensics surfaces it as an incident during the interview, which is evidence for ranking, not enforcement.

classes.title: Files changed well beyond what the task asked for
agentModes: tidies adjacent code while completing a narrow request
reformats a file it only needed one line from

params.note: An expected-file-surface instruction. Probabilistic by construction.

classes.gapNotes: ENFORCEMENT GAP. There is no mechanical statement of what a task asked for, so nothing can measure the overshoot. The only lever is prose, which does not arrive until 0.4.0 and never becomes deterministic.

classes.title: A configuration file rewritten whole instead of amended
agentModes: regenerates a config from its own template rather than editing the existing one

params.signal: whole-file Write to a tracked config file

classes.gapNotes: Not installable at v1: distinguishing a legitimate rewrite from a clobber needs the previous content, and the PostToolUse payload carries no reliable pre-image. jig's own engine solves this for jig-owned files only.

classes.title: A reference to a file or module that is not there
agentModes: cites a path it expected to exist
imports a module it planned to write and did not

params.note: Any test that loads the module fails on a bad import path.

classes.gapNotes: Deterministic for import specifiers from 0.3.0 where eslint-plugin-import is installed. Paths mentioned in prose, in documentation, or in a string argument stay uncovered.
